components.name: Gateway
components.what: NestJS (Fastify) API gateway: simulated login (HS256 JWT, sub = UUID v5 of the email), session validation, correlation IDs, per-IP quota on queue routes, and a fixed-route proxy to every backend. The only public entry for the API.
components.serves: Public: POST /api/v1/auth/login; GET /api/v1/events[/{id}], POST /api/v1/events, PUT .../sales-rules, POST .../publish (Catalog); GET /api/v1/events/{id}/availability (Inventory); POST /api/v1/queue/{id}/join, GET .../status, GET .../stream SSE (Queue); POST/GET /api/v1/orders[/{id}], POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/payment-intents, POST /api/v1/payments/webhook (Orders); GET /mock-gateway/checkout/{paymentId}[/complete] (mock). Internal: none; /internal/v1/** of backends is never reachable. Health: /health/live, /health/ready.

why.note: Login is simulated by the Gateway (no password, no IdP); token keeps an OIDC shape so switching is config.
sub is a UUID v5 of the lower-cased email so the same person keeps the same userId (services/gateway/src/auth/login.service.ts#L26).
X-Queue-Pass is forwarded and logged, never verified.
Per-IP quota counters live in Memorystore; quota fails open while Redis is off (REDIS_URL empty).
The prewarmer owns gateway's service-level minimum instances; Terraform ignores min_instance_count.
Max 3 instances; no DB.
Request timeout 3600 s so the proxied queue SSE stream is not cut every minute (infra/envs/dev/services.tf#L45).
Deployed by digest with blue/green revision tags.

components.name: Catalog
components.what: NestJS service owning events, sectors, sales window and sales rules in PostgreSQL (db-catalog). The only service that decides whether a sale is open (saleState derived from the server clock).
components.serves: Public (via Gateway): GET /api/v1/events?status=PUBLISHED, GET /api/v1/events/{eventId}, POST /api/v1/events, PUT /api/v1/events/{eventId}/sales-rules, POST /api/v1/events/{eventId}/publish. Internal: POST /internal/v1/housekeeping (outbox flush, no sweeps). Also the seed job (three demo events).

why.note: No organizer UI; events come from the seed and Postman/API.
No other service reads this DB; capacity and price reach Inventory and Queue by events.
Outbox flushed after commit, plus the one-minute housekeeping call; no poller.
Max 2 instances x DB pool 2 = 4 connections.
Seed re-emits EventPublished/SalesRulesConfigured on every run so Queue can rebuild its projection in a fresh Memorystore.
Migrations run as Cloud Run job aforo-catalog-migrate before the traffic shift.

components.name: Queue (waiting room)
components.what: NestJS service holding the virtual waiting room in Redis (Memorystore): ordered join (RF-05), batched admission (RF-06), opaque 10-minute pass, and position over SSE. No relational DB.
components.serves: Public (via Gateway): POST /api/v1/queue/{eventId}/join, GET .../status, GET .../stream (SSE). Internal: POST /internal/v1/events/queue-event-published, POST /internal/v1/events/queue-sales-rules (Pub/Sub push). No housekeeping endpoint.

why.note: Store is Memorystore Basic 1 GB, created only for live tests and demos; service boots without it (/health/ready 503, queue routes 500 INTERNAL).
Redis on Cloud Run was superseded by ADR-0001 (no TCP ingress).
Admission is an in-process timer; allowed only because queue has CPU always allocated; a Redis tick lock makes one instance admit per tick.
Admission releases ADMISSION_BATCH_SIZE (500) every ADMISSION_INTERVAL_SECONDS (5).
Admission parameters are env vars, not sales rules.
Position over SSE with 3 s status polling as plan B (implemented in the web).
Pass is opaque, unsigned, never verified downstream.
Prewarmer raises its service-level min instances to 1 during a sales window.

components.name: Orders
components.what: NestJS service owning orders and payments in PostgreSQL (db-orders); orchestrates the purchase saga (reserve -> pay -> confirm or refund) and reaches the payment gateway only through a resilient adapter (ACL).
components.serves: Public (via Gateway): POST /api/v1/orders, GET /api/v1/orders, GET /api/v1/orders/{orderId}, POST /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/payment-intents, POST /api/v1/payments/webhook (HMAC). Internal: POST /internal/v1/events/orders-reservation-expired (push), POST /internal/v1/housekeeping (outbox flush + refund retry sweep).

why.note: Payment mock moved out of Orders into a function, reached through the payment adapter (Anti-Corruption Layer).
Adapter applies timeouts (0.5 s connect, 2 s response), circuit breaker (5 failures, half-open 30 s) and retry with exponential backoff and jitter.
Max 1 instance so the demo shows a single in-memory breaker; pool 3.
Webhook is processed synchronously; refunds retried by housekeeping.
Reservation expiry is never extended; late APPROVED on an expired reservation goes to REFUND_PENDING.
X-Queue-Pass logged (event=queue_pass_received) and ignored.
Replays carry Idempotent-Replayed: true.
Used for the blue/green + migrate-job + rollback evidence.

components.name: Inventory
components.what: NestJS service owning seat availability and reservations in PostgreSQL (db-inventory). The place where a race turns into lost money: the conditional seat decrement guarantees zero overselling (E-02).
components.serves: Public (via Gateway): GET /api/v1/events/{eventId}/availability. Internal: POST /internal/v1/reservations, POST /internal/v1/reservations/{id}/confirm, /release, /expire (Cloud Tasks target), POST /internal/v1/events/inventory-event-published and /inventory-sales-rules (push), POST /internal/v1/housekeeping (expiry sweep + outbox flush).

why.note: The 200-on-10 concurrency test is not cuttable: it is E-02's running evidence.
Expiry by a named Cloud Tasks task per reservation plus a one-minute sweep; expire requires expires_at <= now().
No in-process timers in dev; housekeeping drives the sweep and outbox flush.
3 instances x 80 concurrency x pool 2 = 6 DB connections (aggregate concurrency limit).
No sharding; event_id leads every key so it can be the partition key.
Sectors, prices and rules come from Catalog events, never queried.
Does not verify the queue pass.

components.serves: errors + ProblemJsonFilter (all); correlation middleware (all); JSON logging (all); auth @CurrentUser + ServiceAuthClient ID tokens (all); IdempotencyInterceptor with Idempotent-Replayed (catalog, orders, inventory); envelope buildEnvelope/parse with schemas generated from contracts/events (all producers/consumers, functions via core); OutboxPublisher.flush, no poller (catalog, orders, inventory); HousekeepingModule POST /internal/v1/housekeeping (catalog, orders, inventory); inbox consumeOnce (inventory; orders uses its own InboxRepository; queue uses a Redis Lua script); health live/ready (all); http client 0.5 s / 2 s (orders, gateway); ShutdownService (all services).

why.note: All services are NestJS on Node 24 so one library serves everyone.
Outbox has no poller; flush after commit plus housekeeping.
Replay header implemented in the interceptor.
422 VALIDATION_ERROR vs 400 for malformed bodies and invalid Pub/Sub envelopes.
Functions import only the core entry to keep cold start small (no NestJS).

gotchas: Idempotency is a cache, not a lock: two concurrent first calls both run, so business transactions must be duplicate-safe.

components.name: Purchase happy path (acceptance 1-10)
components.what: The ten acceptance steps of docs/plan/acceptance.md, end to end on dev: login -> catalog -> waiting room -> reserve -> mock payment -> PAID -> my orders -> trace by correlationId.
components.serves: 1. Login with email -> session: app-web /login -> svc-gateway POST /api/v1/auth/login (HS256 JWT). 2. See three published events, open the one on sale: app-web SSR -> svc-gateway -> svc-catalog GET /api/v1/events, /events/{id} (db-catalog); availability from svc-inventory. 3. Join the queue, see position: app-web -> svc-gateway -> svc-queue POST join + SSE stream (data-memorystore); projection fed earlier by catalog events via Pub/Sub. 4. Admitted, buy enabled, pass countdown: svc-queue admission tick (Redis lock) writes the pass; SSE 'admitted' to app-web. 5. Pick sector and two tickets, confirm: app-web /buy -> svc-gateway POST /api/v1/orders with Idempotency-Key and X-Queue-Pass (logged, not verified). 6. Order PENDING_PAYMENT, availability -2: svc-orders -> svc-inventory POST /internal/v1/reservations (seat guard in db-inventory), Cloud Tasks tq-reservation-expiry task enqueued; order row in db-orders. 7. Pay in the mock and return: app-web -> svc-gateway -> svc-orders POST payment-intents -> fn-mock-payment-gateway (ACL + circuit breaker); browser to /mock-gateway/checkout via svc-gateway, 302 back to app-web. 8. PAID in under 5 s: fn-mock-payment-gateway -> tq-payment-webhooks -> svc-gateway -> svc-orders webhook (HMAC, inbox) -> svc-inventory confirm -> order PAID + OrderPaid via outbox to topic-order-paid; app-web polls every 2 s. 9. Listed in GET /orders: app-web /orders -> svc-gateway -> svc-orders GET /api/v1/orders (names from svc-catalog). 10. Follow the correlationId in logs incl. the bus: svc-gateway generates X-Correlation-Id, every service logs it (lib-common), outbox envelopes and Pub/Sub attributes carry it (obs-logging).
